The petitioner is before this Court calling in question the proceedings in C.C.No.2740/2024 pending on the file of the Court of J.M.F.C. (III Court), Mangaluru for offences punishable under Sections 323, 498A of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

sentences.text:
During the pendency of this petition, the parties to the lis have settled the dispute amongst themselves and drawn up a memorandum of settlement, which reads as follows:
"MEMORANDUM OF SETTLEMENT UNDER SECTION 89 OF CPC READ WITH RULES 24 AND 25 OF THE KARNATAKA CIVIL PROCEDURE (MEDIATION)
RULES, 2005.
I. The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 13 (1) (ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 for dissolution of the marriage against the respondent.
II. The aforesaid petition was referred to mediation for resolving the dispute between the parties.
The petitioner, respondent along with their counsels have participated in mediation proceedings.

In the course of mediation, they have resolved their dispute and have agreed to the following terms and conditions:-
NC: 2024:KHC:41051 1.
The Petitioner and respondent are Hindus by religion.

Their marriage was solemnized on 12.05.2017 at Kateel Shree Durgaparameshwari Temple,
Mangaluru as per Hindu rites and customs.
2. Both the parties state that they have no children born to them from their wedlock.
3. Both the aforesaid parties
admit that, due to difference of opinion, severe incompatibility and temperaments the parties are living separately since 14.01.2018.

Inspite of the best efforts made by the elders and the well-wishers, both the petitioner and the respondent could not come together to start their marital life and they state that their marriage is broken down irretrievably.
That there is no chance for reunion; the parties have agreed to get their marriage dissolved by a decree of divorce in their mutual interest.

4. The respondent has agreed to pay an amount of Rs.40,00,000/- (Rupees Forty Lakhs Only) to the petitioner towards permanent alimony/maintenance as full and final settlement by way of demand draft bearing No.142844 dated: 19.07.2024 drawn on Karnataka Bank, Bejai Branch, Mangaluru.
The above said demand draft will be handed over to the petitioner by the respondent before the Hon'ble Court at the time of reporting settlement.

5. Both the parties state that they have already exchanged their valuable articles belonging to each other.
6. Both the parties state that they have no claims of whatsoever nature against each other and also have no claims over movable / immovable properties belonging each other either past, present or future.
Sri Atma Sudhir Shetty vs State Of Karnataka on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46845705/
3 NC: 2024:KHC:41051 7.

entities.text: Atma Sudhir Shetty vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Both the aforesaid parties have entered in to this agreement on their own will and volition, and there is no coercion or undue influence in arriving at this settlement.

8. The petitioner shall withdraw Crl.Misc.No.80/2018 pending before V ACMM., Bengaluru,
R.P.No.121/2024 pending before the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka and agreed to co-operate for quashing of C.C.No.2740/2021 pending before JMFC (III Court).
, Mangaluru as early as possible.
9. Both parties have agreed to close locker No.11 of Canara Bank, Bejai Branch, Mangaluru.
10. Both the aforesaid parties agree not to interfere with each other's personal lives in any manner in future.

III. In view of the aforesaid agreement entered into between the parties, the parties pray that this Court be pleased to dissolve the marriage solemnized on 12.05.2017 at Kateel Shree Durgaparameshwari Temple, Mangaluru by granting a decree of divorce in terms of the aforesaid agreement.
IV. Both the parties have agreed to appear before the Hon'ble Court on 26.07.2024 for passing decree in terms of the agreement."

3. In the light of the settlement arrived at between the parties and the offences not being against the State, I deem it appropriate to accept the same and terminate the proceedings, qua the petitioner.
For the aforesaid reasons, the criminal petition is disposed.

The proceedings in C.C.No.2740/2024 pending on the file of the J.M.F.C. (III Court), Mangaluru, qua the petitioner,
stand quashed.
